sentences.text: The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act preferred by the owner and driver of the motorcycle involved in the fateful accident on 15.10.2018, in which the pillion rider of the motorcycle lost his life, seeks to assail the award dated 07.10.2021 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal insofar as it relates to grant of recovery rights against them.

9. By placing reliance on the decision of this Court in Ramesh Chand Tripathi v. Lily Joshi[FAO No.571/2001, decided on 14.05.2007], learned counsel for the appellants submits that once the motorcycle was insured, it was for the respondent no.3/insurer of the motor cycle to pay compensation on account of the death of the pillion rider and no recovery rights could have been granted against appellants.

entities.text: Ramesh Chand Tripathi v. Lily Joshi[FAO No.571/2001,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She submits that the circular dated 25.03.1977 issued by the Tariff Advisory Committee clearly mandates that, in case, the motorcycle is insured, the compensation towards any injury to the pillion rider will also be borne by the insurance company, which aspect the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate.
10.Upon the appellants taking steps, issue notice to the respondents through all permissible modes.
11.Reply to the applications, if any, be filed within six weeks.
Rejoinder thereto, if any, be filed within four weeks thereafter.

opennyai_summary.issue: The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act preferred by the owner and driver of the motorcycle involved in the fateful accident on 15.10.2018, in which the pillion rider of the motorcycle lost his life, seeks to assail the award dated 07.10.2021 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal insofar as it relates to grant of recovery rights against them.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
9. By placing reliance on the decision of this Court in Ramesh Chand Tripathi v. Lily Joshi[FAO No.571/2001, decided on 14.05.2007], learned counsel for the appellants submits that once the motorcycle was insured, it was for the respondent no.3/insurer of the motor cycle to pay compensation on account of the death of the pillion rider and no recovery rights could have been granted against appellants.
She submits that the circular dated 25.03.1977 issued by the Tariff Advisory Committee clearly mandates that, in case, the motorcycle is insured, the compensation towards any injury to the pillion rider will also be borne by the insurance company, which aspect the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate.
